official.deadline_central_display: 13 October 2026, 17:00 (Paris time) - step 1 submission and registration
official.deadline_note: Step 2 (full proposal) closes in late March 2027, but the exact date and time are given only in the invitation to submit a full proposal sent in February 2027, so it is not yet a fixed calendar deadline. For PRCI collaborations in 'Foreign Lead Agency' modality, a copy of the project must be filed with the foreign agency on the timetable set out in that collaboration's dedicated annex, which differs from the ANR timetable; the French PRCE/PRCI partners must also meet the ANRT 12-month notification deadline for a CIFRE thesis.
official.application_cycle: 2027 edition of the ANR Generic Call for Proposals (AAPG 2027), published 16 July 2026 under the Plan d'action 2027; call text version 1.0
official.status_note: The ANR lists the call as 'Ouvert - 2027' (Open). Opened 16 July 2026 at 09:00 CEST; step 1 submission and registration closes 13 October 2026 at 17:00 CEST. Step 1 results are notified mid-February 2027, step 2 runs from end February 2027 with submission closing end March 2027, and selected JCJC/PRME/PRC/PRCE projects are announced in July 2027, with PRCI results published from September to December 2027.
benefits: Project-based research funding awarded through five funding instruments: JCJC (young researcher), PRME (single-team research project), PRC (collaborative research project), PRCE (collaborative research project with industry) and PRCI (bilateral international collaborative research project)
The JCJC instrument is intended as a springboard for young researchers, thanks to initial ANR support, towards a later European Research Council (ERC) application
Under the PRCE instrument, the ANR and the ANRT operate a simplified joint procedure for a partner company requesting CIFRE PhD funding, with no duplicate scientific assessment by the ANRT
The JCJC and PRCI instruments carry complementary funding opportunities for previously selected projects (Percée JCJC and Jeton MRSEI) to steer teams towards European funding
eligibility: Open to all tenured researchers affiliated with a public or private research organisation, meaning researchers holding a current or forthcoming contract binding them to the managing authority for at least the duration of the project

Regardless of the instrument, the project must include at least one organisation participating in the public research service: either a public-law partner engaged in research and knowledge dissemination (EPST, university, research-focused EPIC, etc.) established in France and applying for ANR funding, or a private-law partner engaged in research and knowledge dissemination with an establishment or branch in France that is not a commercial company

The 2027 AAPG is structured into 57 research themes, each corresponding to a scientific evaluation panel (CES) of the same name; coordinators choose the theme, and therefore the panel, at submission and this choice cannot be modified during the selection process. A project may have a duration of 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54 or 60 months

Submission limits: from the 2027 edition each researcher may participate in a maximum of two submissions to the AAPG and the FRAL SHS call in the same round (a maximum of 1 coordinator role and 1 scientific manager role, or 2 roles), and applicants may not submit as coordinator for two years after being awarded a project in a coordinating role

Instrument-specific rules: JCJC is open only to researchers from public-research-service organisations and the coordinator cannot simultaneously hold JCJC funding and a call with similar objectives (ATIP-Avenir Inserm, Emergence, an ERC Starting or Consolidator Grant, local-authority funding such as Etoile montante); PRME requires a commitment to submit a European call application during the project and up to one year after its scientific end; PRC requires each consortium to include at minimum a young researcher as scientific manager of a partner, or an international partner, or a socio-economic partner; PRCE requires at least one company partner with its registered office or an establishment in France; PRCI requires two coordinators, one French and one foreign
The PRCI ANR-FRQ and ANR-NSF collaborations are suspended for the 2027 edition
requirements: Step 1 submission of the pre-proposal (PRC, PRME, JCJC) and registration of the project (PRCI, PRCE) must be completed on the IRIS submission site by 13 October 2026 at 17:00 Paris time

Coordinators must select the funding instrument and the research theme, and therefore the scientific evaluation panel, at submission; neither the instrument nor the theme can be changed during the selection process, nor can the identity of the coordinator except in cases of force majeure on a specific request to ANR

In step 1, PRCE projects are only required to register their intention to submit: no scientific document is needed, only the online project characterisation form and the online CVs of the coordinators and scientific managers of the partners entered online

Before registering a PRCI project, coordinators must consult the annex dedicated to each bilateral collaboration to confirm that the collaboration is open, its submission modality and the themes concerned

Step 2: coordinators selected at the end of step 1, and coordinators of a PRCI or PRCE project registered in step 1, must submit a full proposal; the step 2 deadline is scheduled for late March 2027 with the exact date and time specified in the invitation

On first login to IRIS, applicants must commit to the IRIS charter and declare any potential use of AI in preparing their scientific project; any project invited to step 2 whose consortium includes at least one commercial company and/or a non-EU partner is subject to an HFDS opinion on the PPST, and a negative opinion prevents funding
documents: AAPG 2027 call text (anr-aapg-2027.pdf / anr-aapg-2027-en.pdf), published 16 July 2026, version 1.0

Guide de l'AAPG 2027 (anr-aapg-2027-guide-v1.0.pdf), published 8 September 2026, the reference document on submission, eligibility, evaluation, selection and funding, together with the FAQ etape 1 (anr-aapg-2027-FAQ-Etp1-V2.0.pdf) covering submission step by step on IRIS
Trame de la pre-proposition / pre-proposal form (anr-aapg-2027-Trame-pre-proposition-V1.0.docx), mandatory for JCJC, PRME and PRC
Completion of a CV for the AAPG call - guidelines (anr-aapg-2027-completion-CV-V1.0-en.pdf), for the CVs completed on the appelsprojetsrecherche.fr portal
Budget annex specific to French partners, mandatory for collaborations in foreign Lead Agency modality (anr-aapg-2027-Annexe-budgetaire-obligatoire-partenaires-fr-Lead.docx)
The annex dedicated to each PRCI bilateral collaboration (DFG, FWF, CNPq, FACEPE, FAPESP, RGC, FNR, NRF, FNS, NSTC), plus the annex for ANR-DGOS co-funding (anr-aapg-2027-cofin-dgos.pdf)
selection_criteria: Scientific excellence is the central principle of evaluation, and the call gives full prominence to fundamental, exploratory and applied research guided by the curiosity of researchers
ANR does not modify the ranked lists provided by the panels and funds the projects by scientific theme according to the budget allocated to each theme
ANR decides whether or not to select a project based on the rankings established by the panels and the budgetary guidelines and priorities approved by the MESR

PRCE step 1 registrations that meet the step 1 eligibility criteria receive an automatic invitation to step 2 without evaluation of the scientific value of the registration by the scientific evaluation panels
For PRCI, selection for funding is made by joint agreement of the two funding agencies, and each agency funds the teams in its own country according to its own funding procedures

Projects ranked on the 2026 complementary list and resubmitted at step 1 are automatically invited to step 2 without panel evaluation, provided they have the same coordinator, the same funding instrument, the same title and a comparable consortium and are complete by the step 1 closing date
coverage: Project-based research funding awarded through the JCJC, PRME, PRC, PRCE and PRCI instruments; the call text publishes no per-project amount, and eligible cost categories are defined in the ANR financial regulations rather than in the call text
Under the PRCE instrument, ANR funding can cover a partner company's CIFRE PhD, applied for through the simplified joint ANR-ANRT procedure
Under the PRCI instrument, each funding agency funds the teams of its own country according to its own funding procedures, so only the French teams are funded by the ANR
A preciput is paid in addition to project funding to the managing and hosting establishments of selected projects, at rates decided by the ANR Board (published on the ANR financial regulations page)
application_method: Create or use an account on the appelsprojetsrecherche.fr portal and the IRIS submission site, and complete the CVs online for the coordinator and the scientific managers of the partners
Choose the funding instrument (JCJC, PRME, PRC, PRCE or PRCI) and the research theme, and therefore the scientific evaluation panel, that best matches the scientific objectives of the project
For JCJC, PRME and PRC, submit the pre-proposal using the published template on IRIS before 13 October 2026 at 17:00 Paris time
For PRCE, complete only the online project characterisation form and the online CVs on IRIS by the same deadline; this registration, if eligible, gives an automatic invitation to step 2

For PRCI, check the dedicated annex of the intended bilateral collaboration to confirm it is open, its modality and its themes, then register the project on IRIS in ANR Lead Agency or non-Lead Agency modality
On invitation in February 2027, submit the full proposal on IRIS by the step 2 deadline given in the invitation (scheduled late March 2027)
official.application_route: Two-step online submission on the ANR's IRIS portal: step 1 pre-proposal (JCJC/PRME/PRC) or registration (PRCE/PRCI) by 13 October 2026 at 17:00 Paris time, then, on invitation, a step 2 full proposal due late March 2027.
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship or nationality rule is published. Eligibility rests on affiliation: the coordinator must be a tenured researcher holding a current or forthcoming contract binding them to the managing authority for at least the duration of the project, and the project must include at least one organisation participating in the French public research service (or a non-commercial private-law partner with an establishment or branch in France).
official.international_eligibility: Yes, in defined forms. PRCI is specifically designed for bilateral international collaboration and requires two coordinators, one French and one foreign; PRC consortia may include an international partner as one of the profiles satisfying the new PRC eligibility criteria; PRME commits the coordinator to submitting a European call application. For PRCI, the foreign partner's own agencies assess and fund their national teams.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The project must be submitted under one of the 57 research themes, each mapped to a scientific evaluation panel; themes cover 38 axes in 7 disciplinary fields (Environmental Sciences, Materials and Engineering Sciences, Life Sciences, Digital Sciences and Mathematics, Physics of Matter and Sciences of the Universe, Humanities and Social Sciences, and their cross-cutting issues) and 19 trans- or interdisciplinary cross-cutting axes. Priorities include AI, SHS at interfaces, quantum technologies, neurodevelopmental disorders, therapeutic proof-of-concept in rare diseases, mathematics, exploitation of research-infrastructure data, mental health, and PFAS (new for 2027). PRCE requires at least one French company partner, and PRCI requires one of the listed bilateral partner agencies.
official.research_requirement: A research project is required in all cases. In step 1, JCJC, PRME and PRC require a pre-proposal on the published template, while PRCE requires only the online project characterisation form and CVs, and PRCI requires registration plus, in some modalities, a copy filed with the foreign lead agency. Step 2 requires a full scientific proposal; a data management plan and a TRL/SRL positioning (used informationally, not in evaluation) are part of the project description.
official.duration: A project submitted to the AAPG call may have a duration of 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54 or 60 months.
official.description: The Generic Call for Proposals (AAPG) is the main call of the French National Research Agency. It is open to all scientific communities and all public or private stakeholders involved in French research, and supports project-based research across all scientific fields and disciplines, giving full prominence to fundamental, exploratory and finalised research guided by the curiosity of researchers. The 2027 edition mobilises five funding instruments across 57 research themes.

verification.notes: Checked the ANR call page (FR and EN), the official AAPG 2027 call text v1.0 of 16 July 2026 downloaded from anr.fr, the Plan d'action 2027 page and press release, the funding instruments page and the financial regulations page. The deadline, calendar, five instruments, 57 themes, eligibility rules, submission limits, documents and PRCI modalities are all published and quoted from those pages. The call text and every other ANR page publish no per-project award amount, no currency, no funding period, no tuition/living/travel coverage statement and no English language requirement, so those fields are null rather than inferred; the AAPG is a project grant to an institution, not a personal scholarship, so no amount should be recorded.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a scholarship you can apply for as an individual: it is the ANR's flagship call for research project funding, submitted by a coordinator through the IRIS portal, and the money goes to the institution, not to a person. If you are a doctoral student hoping to be funded, your only realistic route in is being recruited onto a selected project, most often through a doctoral contract or, under PRCE, a CIFRE PhD with a partner company. The two hard gates are the 13 October 2026 step 1 deadline and the fact that your project must sit under one of 57 research themes with a matching coordinator profile. Budget wise, the call text deliberately publishes no award amount, so plan the budget with your institution's research support office against the ANR financial regulations' eligible cost categories rather than against a published ceiling.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Tenured researchers at a French public research institution who can assemble a consortium and a credible pre-proposal in the next few days, and who are willing to treat the grant as a stepping stone to a Horizon Europe application.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm today whether you still have a step 1 slot left: from the 2027 edition you may take part in at most two AAPG/FRAL submissions in the round, and you cannot coordinate again for two years after coordinating a funded project
Check your own 'limit of coordination' status before building a consortium, because an ineligible coordinator sinks the whole file at step 1

Pick the funding instrument before writing anything, and read the instrument description in the 2027 call text in full even if you resubmitted last year, since instrument expectations changed for PRC and PRME; do the same for your research theme description, whose scope has evolved between editions

Verify your IRIS and appelsprojetsrecherche.fr accounts and the online CVs of the coordinator and every partner scientific manager now, since the same person may not be scientific manager for two partners and CVs are completed on a separate portal

For PRC, assemble the qualifying profile in writing early (a young researcher as partner scientific manager, or an international partner, or a socio-economic partner), because this is now an eligibility criterion and not just a scoring point
For PRCE, name the French company partner and decide at submission whether you are requesting a CIFRE thesis, since the ANRT request window closes 12 months after expenditure becomes eligible
common_rejection_risks: Being ruled ineligible at step 1 on the submission limits or the coordination-career gap, which removes you before any scientific reading
For PRC, failing the new consortium composition rule: without a young researcher scientific manager, an international partner or a socio-economic partner, the file is not eligible at all
Choosing a research theme or instrument that no longer matches the project, since neither can be changed once submitted and mismatches are a classic cause of poor panel alignment

For PRCE, a negative HFDS opinion on the protection of scientific and technical heritage (PPST): every PRCE project invited to step 2 is systematically reviewed, and a negative opinion blocks funding outright
For PRCI, registering under a suspended collaboration: the ANR-FRQ and ANR-NSF routes are suspended for 2027, so such files have nowhere to go

A PRME project where the coordinator cannot realistically file a Horizon Europe application during the project or within one year of its scientific end, since proof of that submission is a condition of payment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The call text publishes no per-project amount, no funding period and no cost-category list, so there is no published ceiling to budget against and nothing in the catalogue should be read as a typical award. Eligible cost categories and the aid rates (real-cost versus flat-rate aid) live in the ANR financial regulations, and a selected project also attracts a preciput paid to the managing and hosting establishments rather than to the team, so your institution's research support service must model the request and identify what stays with the partners. Treat any salary, overhead, consumable or mobility line that is not an eligible cost as something your institution and partners carry themselves.
document_audit: The PRCE step 1 trap runs the other way from what applicants expect: no scientific document is required at all, only the online characterisation form and the CVs, and that thin registration is still automatically invited to step 2
CVs are not uploaded as files: they are completed on the appelsprojetsrecherche.fr portal, so a late or half-filled CV blocks the submission while the science looks finished
For a PRCI collaboration in foreign Lead Agency modality, the budget annex for French partners is mandatory, not optional

Each PRCI bilateral collaboration has its own annex, and the annex, not the call text, is what confirms whether the collaboration is open, its modality and its themes; some were only published after 8 September 2026 as collaborations were validated
PRCI requires two named coordinators, one French and one foreign, and the same person may not act as scientific manager for two partners within the same project
In any difference of interpretation the French version of the call text prevails, and the IRIS charter and AI-use declaration are required at first login, so build time for both into submission day
alerts: Step 1 closes 13 October 2026 at 17:00 Paris time: the step 2 date is not fixed in advance and is only communicated in the February 2027 invitation, so do not build a work plan on the 'late March 2027' placeholder

The ANR-FRQ (Franco-Quebec) and ANR-NSF (Franco-American) PRCI collaborations are both suspended for the 2027 edition; the ANR-NSF notice was updated as late as 7 October 2026, so re-check the call page before registering

If your PRCI project is selected at the 2026 edition you must cancel your 2027 registration, or your JCJC/PRME/PRC submission or PRCE registration, by email to aapg.science@anr.fr, and 2026 PRCI results only arrive between September and December 2026
Panel chairs must not be contacted by applicants under any circumstances; the list of 2027 panel chairs is published before evaluation, expected November 2026
The two-submission cap and the two-year coordination gap are new for 2027, so rules you applied last year no longer hold
A step 1 pass is not a funding decision: ANR funds theme by theme according to the budget allocated to each theme, so a strong project can still fall outside the available theme budget
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register online on IRIS, complete the online CVs on the appelsprojetsrecherche.fr portal, file the step 1 pre-proposal or registration before 13 October 2026 at 17:00 Paris time, then wait for the February 2027 invitation to file the step 2 full proposal.
